newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Crane says Q1 profits have risen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Crane says Q1 profits have risen.

text.p: Building products group G.E. Crane Holdings Ltd said on Friday that net profit in the first quarter of 1996/97 was above last year's level.
Chairman Evan Cameron also told shareholders at the annual meeting that the full year net profit should be supported by productivity improvements, cost savings, and export sales.
In late August, the company reported a fall in 1995/96 (July/June) net profit to A$20.54 million from A$24.22 million a year earlier.

Cameron said Crane saw little chance of an upturn in market demand and believed that any strengthening in the Australian building industry was likely to be modest and not occur until late in the year.

"So while the outlook in terms of sales and volumes is subdued, we believe our profit result will be supported by continuing productivity improvements, an on-going push in exports of our manufactured products and rationalisation benefits and cost-savings from the acquisitions of Raymor and Alumex," he said.
"In the first three months of this year, after tax profit is higher than in the corresponding period last year," he said.
"In the metals manufacturing group, both sales volumes and earnings before interest and tax are higher than the previous corresponding period," Cameron said.
"The merchandising group has a similar story, with sales volumes and earnings before interest and tax ahead of last year," he said.
"Based on current information, we expect profits for the current year to exceed last year's profits," he said, without quantifying the increase.
Crane shares were 25 cents higher at A$10.25 at 11.18 a.m. (0118 GMT).
